subject: Discovery Recap: Private/VPC options for FinHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Murray <alex.murray@finhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 20:10:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery Recap: Private/VPC options for FinHealth

Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points you raised
- Regulated workloads (PHI & financial data) — you need strict data residency and auditability.
- Network constraints — FinHealth runs most ML workloads in a private VPC and has strict egress restrictions; some teams run in an on-prem data center.
- KMS/HSM requirement — customer-managed keys and hardware-backed key storage for model encryption at rest.
- Air-gap consideration — the security team asked whether we can support an offline / air-gapped on-prem deployment for highly regulated environments.

Current stack you shared
- Kubernetes on-prem for core services, AWS GovCloud for some analytics workloads.
- Existing ML infra: model training in-house, limited serving (CPU-based), using an internal NFS for artifact storage.
- Identity: Okta SSO; networking via transit VPC with strict firewall rules.

Success criteria you called out
- Private deployment that can live inside customer VPC (or fully on-prem) with no outbound dependencies.
- Integrates with your KMS/HSM for key management and supports key rotation/audit logs.
- Meets SOC 2 / security questionnaire requirements and provides logs/audit trail for tokens and access.
- Predictable latency: <150ms p95 for inference in your baseline workloads.

What Redwood can offer (high level)
- Redwood Private (VPC & on-prem): private control plane option and an air-gap capable on-prem package — we’ll validate air-gap scope in the technical deep-dive.
- KMS integrations: support for customer-managed KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, external HSM via PKCS#11) and encryption at rest for model artifacts and caches.
- Audit & logging: configurable audit logs, token-level tracing, and optional longer retention for compliance teams.

Agreed next steps
1) I’ll share a 1-page architecture sketch showing deployment options (attached).
2) Tech deep-dive: schedule a call next week with your infra & security leads + our infra/ops engineers to validate air-gap requirements and network flows.
3) Share SOC2 artifacts and answer the security questionnaire you mentioned — you can send the questionnaire to infosec@redwood.com.
4) Provide a ballpark pricing and mutual action plan for an on-prem / private deployment after the deep-dive.

Attachments: redwood_private_arch_diagram_v1.pdf (high-level sketch), meeting_recording_20260308.mp4 (call recording).

If any of the above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll work with Rishi to prepare the MAP and draft a technical agenda.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Murray <alex.murray@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Security <infosec@finhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Private/VPC options for FinHealth

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap, that captures the conversation well. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Air-gap: Our risk team will likely require either a fully isolated on-prem deployment (no outbound) or a highly controlled egress path that can be reviewed. We should treat the fully air-gapped option as the gating scenario for our most regulated workloads.
2) KMS/HSM: We use an internal HSM that exposes a PKCS#11 interface; we’ll need to confirm that Redwood Private can call into an on-prem HSM or a proxy.
3) Latency target: the 150ms p95 is a good baseline, but if the model size changes we need to understand scaling/cost tradeoffs.

I’m attaching our security questionnaire and a network diagram of the environment to help frame the deep-dive.

Next steps from our side: I’ll loop in our infra lead (cc’d) once we have potential times. We’ll also share any additional compliance artifacts you need.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Murray
SVP, Platform Engineering | FinHealth
alex.murray@finhealth.com | (617) 555-0199
